cycles.rationale: The sphere is stable with zero drift and spin but has very large full-orientation and X/Y error, so the large sphere orientation escape is the best initial probe.

Full orientation error is still very large with a significant sphere Y component and drift is stable, so I will try an untried sphere Y-orientation probe instead of repeating action_25 after its yaw change had the wrong sign.

action_24 was the most effective last cycle, reducing rot_dist by 0.161 rad and tilt while producing the needed negative yaw, with low drift and stable spin, so continuing it is preferred over switching contact groups.

action_24 has decayed and the grasp is stable with low spin, while X/Y tilt error remains large, so I will probe an untried WRJ0 three-axis orientation correction rather than repeat a stalled thumb cycle.

Tilt (X/Y) error dominates at 64.8 deg and action_18 (WRJ0 direction A) just increased full-orientation error, so with drift low and spin moderate I try the untried opposite-direction WRJ0 probe action_19 to reduce the X/Y error.

Orientation error is still very large (rot_dist 1.788 rad, tilt 68.8 deg) with low drift and low spin, and action_25 is the only untried-stall-free option that previously gave positive rot_dist gain (+0.079 rad) and the largest tilt reduction (+12.4 deg), so repeat the large sphere orientation escape rather than stalled action_24 or harmful probes 18/19.

Full orientation error is still very large (rot_dist 1.47 rad) with stable grasp and moderate spin, and action_25 just produced the largest gain (0.3177 rad) reducing all XYZ error components with a positive trend and only one consecutive use, so continuing the large sphere orientation escape is warranted.

action_25 has decayed after repeated uses (last rot_dist gain -0.0815, stalled), while the large X/Y tilt error (-36/-46 deg) persists and the failed WRJ0 probes (18/19) suggest trying the untried WRJ1-based contact-changing three-axis probe action_21 to attack tilt from a different contact group.
The sphere is stable with low residual spin, and action_24 has the best measured tendency to reduce both dominant negative X/Y errors while preserving a small positive Z correction.
Tilt remains large (X=-28.9,Y=-46.6) and action_24 is the only recent primitive with positive full-orientation and Y gains, so continue it once rather than switching to a stalled or harmful probe.

Full orientation error is still huge (1.571 rad) with significant sphere Y error (-46.7 deg) while action_24 and action_25 have both stalled after repetition, so switch to the untried sphere Y-orientation probe in opposed direction A with a braced fore/middle contact group.
Positive yaw and large negative X/Y tilt remain while drift is stable; action_22 (direction A) worsened rot_dist and Y, so I’m trying the untried opposed sphere-Y probe action_23.

Recent thumb/WRJ1 probes (21-24) have steadily worsened rot_dist to 1.67 rad with large X/Y tilt (59 deg) and are stalled, so I am switching to an untried different-contact-group three-axis probe (little-finger/thumb escape) targeting the significant X/Y error while drift remains low and stable.

Full orientation error is very large (1.73 rad) with stable grasp and low spin, while recent sphere/thumb probes (20/22/23/24) and stalled action_25 have been increasing rot_dist, so I switch to an untried coarse-rotation primitive from a different ring-finger contact group to seek a fresh large correction.

The +94 deg yaw error needs negative yaw, but every recently tried primitive produced positive yaw and steadily increased rot_dist to 1.86 rad; action_25 is the only measured action with negative yaw and correctly signed X/Y/Z gains (positive mean rot_dist gain) for this very large sphere orientation error.

Error is still very large (rot_dist 1.701 rad) with stable low drift, and action_25 just produced the best full-orientation gain (+0.160 rad) with all XYZ gains aligned to the signed error components and a positive trend, so continue the effective coarse escape rather than switching or finishing.

Full orientation error is still very large (rot_dist 1.417 rad) and action_25 is the only primitive with strong, improving gains (last rot_dist gain +0.2837 rad, tilt gain +22.9 deg, yaw delta -10.955 deg) with stable drift, so continue it rather than switching to harmful or untried actions.

Full orientation error is still very large (rot_dist 1.2497) with stable grasp (drift_xy 0.0056) and moderate spin, and action_25 remains the only primitive with strong positive gains (last +0.1676 rad, well above the 0.01 stall threshold) while correctly driving the dominant positive Z/yaw error down, so continuing the large sphere escape is warranted despite the slowly decaying trend.

rot_dist_rad is still very large (1.168) and action_25 remains the only primitive with consistent positive geodesic gain (last +0.0817 rad, recent3 +0.1777), above the 0.01 stall threshold, with moderate spin so no hold is needed; I will keep monitoring the rising tilt and borderline drift.

action_25 has stalled (5 straight uses, last rot_dist gain -0.0256 rad) and must be abandoned; the dominant residual is the +51 deg Y/tilt error on a sphere, so switch contact group to the thumb-based sphere-Y probe action_24, which has the only positive mean full-orientation gain (~0.05 rad) among the Y probes.
Positive yaw error needs negative yaw; reverse-thumb action_24 worsened and action_25 has stalled, while drift and spin are stable, so try the untried standard thumb coarse rotation.

action_25 has stalled and is worsening tilt while the last two probes (24, 05) increased rot_dist, so with large 3-axis error and stable drift I switch to an untried different contact group (wrist+fore/middle) coarse probe to seek negative yaw without further degrading X/Y.

Full-orientation error is still very large (1.53 rad) with dominant +Z yaw needing negative rotation and stable low drift; action_25 has decayed after 8 uses (negative trend, last gain <0.01) and recent probes 24/05 worsened error while 06 was marginal, so I switch to an untried coarse-rotation primitive from a different contact group suited to large error with stable contact.

The error is still very large and Z-dominated (err +78 deg, rot_dist 1.43 rad) while prior yaw/coarse actions have stalled or worsened yaw, so with drift low and stable I switch to an untried alternate-contact escape to refresh the contact pattern and seek a negative-yaw gain.

Error is still large (rot_dist 1.358 rad, dominated by +Z/yaw) and the grasp is stable; action_04 was just helpful (rot_dist gain +0.0765, yaw delta -6.802 in the needed negative direction, Z-component gain +7.28) with only one consecutive use and gain well above 0.5 deg, so continuing it exploits the current effective contact before switching.

The grasp is stable and full orientation error is still large, so after two little-finger cycles I switch to the forefinger coarse primitive that previously produced the strongest rot_dist and tilt reduction despite a small adverse yaw.

The last action_02 worsened rot_dist and X-tilt, while action_04 is the only recently reliable primitive (2/2 helpful, mean rot_dist gain +0.068 rad, negative yaw that reduces the +66 deg Z error with component gains matching the positive XYZ errors); drift is low and it is not yet overused, so I return to it.

action_04 is still producing consistent full-orientation gains (last rot_dist gain 0.0602 rad, recent3 mean 0.0653) with stable drift and large remaining error, so continuing it is preferable to switching while it remains effective.

Full orientation error is still very large (rot_dist 1.228 rad) and action_04's gains are decaying (0.076→0.044) after four uses, so I switch contact groups to the large sphere-orientation escape primitive, which has the largest mean rot_dist gain (0.123 rad) and matches the very-large-error scenario while spin is moderate and the object is not dropped.

err_deg is large and positive requiring negative yaw, and action_25 just produced the strongest recent full-orientation gain (rot_dist +0.0657 rad) with positive gains on all three XYZ components, a negative yaw delta matching the needed direction, low spin, and a positive trend without stall, so continuing it is best while rot_dist_rad remains far above the 0.1 success threshold.
The sphere still has large full-orientation error and positive yaw error, while action_25 is producing the best recent negative-yaw and rot_dist gains without signs of stall or unsafe drift.

action_25 has been used three times and its last run made rot_dist and tilt much worse, while drift_xy (0.0326) exceeds the 0.02 reseat threshold, so I switch to an untried position-recovery/contact-escape primitive to recenter and refresh the grasp before re-attacking the large orientation error.

With large positive yaw error and significant tilt but low drift, action_04 is the best available contact-changing rotation: it has reliably produced negative yaw and positive full-orientation gains without recent overuse.

The error is dominated by a large +Y tilt component (42.7 deg, tilt 43.3) with stalled action_25/action_04, and action_02 has a positive mean rot_dist gain (+0.031 rad), a strong +Y gain (+11.2 deg) matching the current +Y error, and only two prior uses so it is not stalled.

Full orientation error is still large (1.206 rad) with 37 deg tilt, and action_16 produced the best recent combined effect (+0.030 rad orientation gain, +22.3 deg tilt reduction, +0.024 m recentering) without stalling, unlike repeated action_25.

The negative-yaw producers (action_25, action_04) and recent rotations have stalled with declining/negative rot_dist gains while tilt keeps worsening, and drift is low, so I switch to an untried contact-refresh (different contact group) to re-form the grasp and let the moderate sphere spin settle before the next correction.

Full orientation error is still very large with low drift, and action_25 is the sphere large-orientation escape with the strongest measured negative-yaw/Z correction despite needing monitoring for decay.
Drift_xy is above 0.02 m and full-orientation progress has stalled, so an untried recentering/contact-changing recovery is preferable before further rotation probes.

Sphere with very large full-orientation error (1.2504 rad), stable low drift, and action_25 has the best episode record (10/12 helpful, positive rot_dist gain, negative yaw matching the large positive Z error) while not being stalled or consecutive.

action_25 is overused and decaying (recent3 rot gain ~0.004) while worsening the large +Y/tilt error and pushing drift up, so I switch to a different thumb contact group targeting the +41 deg Y component whose prior use gave correct-sign Y gain.

The error is still large with positive yaw requiring negative yaw, drift is stable, and action_25 remains the most reliable negative-yaw/full-orientation gainer whose last use still improved rot_dist by 0.066 rad.

rot_dist_rad is still very large (1.26) and action_25 is the only primitive with a consistently positive full-orientation gain, so I continue it while drift remains bounded rather than switching to probes that have repeatedly increased rot_dist.

rot_dist_rad (1.2236) is far from the 0.1 success threshold and action_25 is the only primitive with consistently positive full-orientation gain (last +0.0366 rad, mean +0.0823) that is still above the 0.01 stall floor with only 2 consecutive uses, so I continue the proven large-error reducer rather than switching to Y-probes whose net rot_dist gains were negative.

Full orientation error is still very large (1.187 rad) and action_25 remains the only primitive with a strong helpful track record (12/16, mean rot_dist gain +0.0795 rad, mean yaw −5.99 deg matching the needed negative yaw); its latest gain (+0.0364 rad) is still above the 0.01 stall threshold, so continuing is justified despite three uses.

action_25 is still the only consistently helpful primitive (last rot_dist gain 0.0571 rad with positive trend, not stalled), its negative-yaw signature matches the dominant +57.8 deg Z error, and recent uses also reduced the X/Y components, while drift (0.0248 m) remains well below the drop threshold.

Full orientation error is still very large (1.048 rad) and action_25 remains highly effective with last rot_dist gain 0.0824 rad and positive trend, so continuing the large sphere orientation escape is warranted since drift is stable and no fine correction is yet sufficient.

action_25 has decayed and last cycle worsened rot_dist (-0.16 rad) and tilt (-28.6 deg), so I switch contact groups to a three-axis probe whose measured gains (X negative, Y positive, near-zero Z) best match the current error vector [-25.8, +49.9, +40.3] dominated by tilt.

Z yaw error (+57 deg) is the dominant component and needs negative yaw; action_25 has stalled/destabilized, while action_04 is a proven negative-yaw producer (5/5 helpful, mean rot_dist gain +0.041 rad) from a different contact group than the just-used action_21.

rot_dist is large (1.18) with significant Y/tilt error, and action_21 most recently gave the best full-orientation gain (+0.0895 rad) with a positive trend and big tilt/position improvement, while the LFJ4-based actions 25/04 have stalled or worsened rot_dist.
The last two rotation attempts made rot_dist worse while drift and spin are low, so a brief fore/middle/ring contact refresh with prior positive rot gain and negative yaw is appropriate.
